sizeMatchedRandomReference.statistic: Mean answer-gist cosine in127uniformly sampled distinct-upload candidate pairs; count-matched descriptive baseline, not a calibrated null.

commonSupportStandardization.weightDefinition: Within the bins containing both quarantine strata, weight each bin by its pooled neighbor-pair count, then apply the identical weights to the separate group means.
limitations: Quarantine is constructed from question similarity; unsupported high-similarity bins cannot identify a cross-quarantine comparison.
The retained common-support pool differs from all127neighbors. Standardization does not replace the original all-neighbor/cross-group descriptive summaries.
Coarse bins leave within-bin question-similarity, length, topic and source selection differences. No causal session-reuse or answer-agreement claim follows.
Neighbor pairs share candidates/uploads; no independent-pair confidence interval or inferential p-value is reported.

benchmarkGuard.rule: Link uploads if any exactly normalized question repeats, any question cosine>=0.80, OR at least three cross-upload question pairs cosine>=0.40. Connected components are conservative quarantine groups, not proven original-session families.

representationNuisance.partialRankDefinition: Pearson correlation of title and caption rank residuals after separate OLS projection on intercept and ranked nuisance variables. No p-value or independent-pair uncertainty interval.

titleCosine.method: OLS projection on intercept, absolute log duration ratio, mean log duration in minutes, and absolute log caption word-count ratio; within-minus-between means of residual cosine. Descriptive conditioning, not a causal or speaker effect.

captionCosine.method: OLS projection on intercept, absolute log duration ratio, mean log duration in minutes, and absolute log caption word-count ratio; within-minus-between means of residual cosine. Descriptive conditioning, not a causal or speaker effect.

leaveOnePublisherOut.meaning: Deterministic influence range, not a confidence interval.

model.parameterScale: 0.5B family; bounded CPU baseline, not established state of the art

interpretation: These are eight held-out AI-digest reconstruction questions and two deliberately unsupported controls, not a model quality ranking.
Train-only RAG intentionally excludes the target source group and answer; this is sparse-source transfer, not an ordinary answer-present RAG comparison.
Token F1 measures lexical overlap. Supplied-label membership does not establish entailment or factual correctness.
Control counts require the literal INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE marker. A spaced refusal such as Insufficient evidence. scores zero; this is formatting compliance, not general refusal accuracy.
The 40-new-token generation cap and 192-token training cap can affect lexical scores; length and citation-normalized sensitivities remain separate checks.
Observed split quarantine does not rule out pretrained-model contamination or unknown source-session overlap.
One LoRA closed control output invents an exact studio temperature (23°C); this is a concrete unsupported response, not inferred from lexical scores.
benchmarkAudit.adapterVerification: Portable archive/member hashes verified; adapter weight bytes match the original training receipt. Package README/config normalization is described by its separate manifest. No external model cache is required for this audit.

limitations: AI digest questions and answer gists are a one-practitioner paraphrase source, not literal turns or independently verified answers.
Pair scores share questions, uploads and publishers; numerical association is descriptive, not independent human evidence.
Question lexical components and quarantine links do not establish semantic equivalence or repeated original sessions.
The count-matched random reference does not match publisher, format or word-length distributions and is not a calibrated null.
Partial ranks and residual cosine condition on observed length variables only; they do not establish causal mediation or isolate speaker identity.
Frozen caption/title vectors use the historical masked MiniLM representations; no new encoder was executed.

limits: The broader refusal pattern was defined after output inspection and is not human refusal or correctness annotation.
The positive-control source answers are intentionally supplied from training; their overlap/citation scores are not held-out generalization.
The twelve text-label examples are balanced on a dictionary heuristic; method concordance is not accuracy or corpus prevalence.
All nine parsed themes collapse to contact_forecast; do not use this failed probe as empirical theme distribution.
No exact answer evidence spans passed the specified source-substring rule.
Citation-stripped overlap preserves the original scores as separate metrics; no model parameters are optimized on this diagnostic.
Generation cap hits document censoring; no longer-budget generation experiment was executed.

optionOrder.interpretation: Observed prompt sensitivity; no reversed valid output selects the new first option, so a simple deterministic first-option-copy account does not fit this probe. No annotation accuracy is established.

currentFamily.interpretation: Same-item schema and quotation-compliance comparison across different architectures/tokenizers/runtimes; not semantic-label accuracy, parameter-scale causality, held-out QA improvement or general model ranking.

limits: Original outputs, original dictionary labels and the five-arm held-out pilot remain preserved.
Paired option changes use only items parsed under both prompts; all parse failures remain visible.
The stricter conditional pattern is a post-hoc lexical sensitivity, not a corrected human reference.
All models can collapse to one conditional label; dictionary concordance is not annotation accuracy.
The current-family model receives text only. No image, video, speech, GPU or current-family fine-tuning experiment is implied.
A shared96-token cap is not an identical word/context budget across tokenizers.

model.parameterScale: 0.5B family; bounded CPU baseline, not established state of the art

split.sourceScope: 949 inherited AI digest pairs; Darryl Anka/Bashar context only
split.groupRule: Union upload IDs if any exact normalized question, any question cosine>=0.80, or >=3 cross-upload retrieval pairs at cosine>=0.40; conservative proxy, not known original sessions
split.ragCorpus: training examples only; no heldout question or answer provided as RAG evidence

training.comparisonLimit: No GPU vs CPU timing comparison was executed

metrics.meanTokenF1: Multiset alphanumeric-token overlap with heldout AI digest gist; lexical reconstruction, not factual correctness
metrics.validCitationRate: Fraction of heldout outputs naming at least one supplied evidence label; ID membership only, not entailment
metrics.meanSeconds: Wall time per response including query retrieval when used, prompt tokenization and generation; excludes one-time model loading/index fitting
metrics.abstentionRateOnControls: Fraction of two unanswerable studio-temperature/audio-hash probes explicitly emitting INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE

limitations: Eight heldout questions and two controls are a pilot, not a reliable comparative ranking.
All training and reference targets are model-generated digest paraphrases from one practitioner context.
Proxy source families reduce known question/repost leakage but cannot establish independent original sessions.
RAG searches only the 48 training examples; retrieval evidence may not answer a heldout question.
Token overlap and source-label membership do not validate semantic agreement, provenance entailment or factual truth.
One short CPU LoRA epoch is an adaptation smoke test, not an optimized fine-tuning study.
CUDA/GPU comparison is unavailable; CPU latency includes this shared machine and short outputs.
No human construct labels, speech transcription or new multi-practitioner answers were created.

modelProtocol.source: 949 existing AI-generated digest Q&A paraphrases, Darryl Anka/Bashar context only
modelProtocol.groupRule: Quarantine upload pairs connected by any identical normalized question, any question cosine >=0.80, or at least three question retrieval pairs at cosine >=0.40
modelProtocol.groupCaveat: Source-family proxies are not verified original-session identities and cannot rule out unknown repost or pretraining overlap
modelProtocol.ragIndex: Only the 48 selected training examples; heldout answer gists are never RAG evidence

ragRetrieval.method: word unigram/bigram English-stop-word sublinear TF-IDF, smooth IDF, L2 normalization

baseModel.interpretation: Small feasible CPU baseline, not established current state of the art

metrics.tokenOverlapF1: Multiset lowercase alphanumeric token overlap with heldout AI-generated answer gist; no factual-correctness inference
metrics.citationMembership: Output contains a supplied [D1]/[D2] label; syntactic membership only, not entailment
metrics.unsupportedControlAbstention: Exact INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE marker on two questions requiring absent studio-temperature or unpublished audio-hash evidence
metrics.latency: Wall-clock generation/response time on this shared CPU machine, not a hardware benchmark ranking

modelProtocol.currentFamilyFeasibility: Inspect official Qwen3/Qwen3.5 metadata and attempt a separate Qwen3.5-0.8B text-only smoke test after verified downloads; no global SOTA or image capability claim
modelProtocol.gpuComparison: Unsupported on this machine: no CUDA device exposed. Do not manufacture GPU throughput or GPU training metrics.

figures.title: Question and answer lexical resemblance
figures.caption: 127 cross-upload question neighbors at cosine≥.40 among 949 digest candidates. Independent question and answer TF–IDF vocabularies; neither score measures answer agreement. Quarantine groups use conservative lexical-source links, not verified original sessions. Pair entries share candidates/uploads and are dependent; the source-derived question wording can itself be normalized by the digest generator.

figures.title: Lexical-neighbor connectivity depends on the cutoff
figures.caption: Graph vertices are 949 digest question candidates; edges connect different uploads meeting each lexical cosine threshold. Isolated candidates remain in the denominator. At .40, 178 candidates participate in non-singleton components and the largest contains 15 candidates; components are lexical neighborhoods, not validated semantic topics or independent source families.

figures.title: Representation association after length conditioning
figures.caption: Identical 25 uploads from 14 publishers yield 300 dependent pairs (11 within, 289 between). Right: title/caption rank residuals after separate linear projection on ranked absolute log duration ratio, mean log duration and absolute log caption word-count ratio. Their Pearson correlation defines the reported partial rank association. This is descriptive conditioning, not causal mediation; publisher-omission partial correlations range −.026 to .207, not a confidence interval.

figures.title: Conservative source grouping changes the compared pairs
figures.caption: 67 Q&A-bearing uploads form 55 conservative quarantine groups. Links use any exact normalized question, any question cosine≥.80, or at least three cross-upload question pairs≥.40. These are leakage guards, not established recording identities. Among 127 question-neighbor pairs, 70 are within a quarantine group and 57 cross groups. Boxplots are empirical distributions with dependent pairs, not confidence intervals or measured agreement.

figures.title: Lexical reconstruction and strict control-marker compliance
figures.caption: Actual Qwen2.5-0.5B CPU pilot: eight held-out digest questions and two deliberately unsupported controls per arm. Left dots are individual token-F1 values, diamonds are arithmetic means; no uncertainty interval or reliable ranking is implied. Gold counts literal INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE; when blue bars are present, they count a broader post-hoc refusal phrase rule defined after inspecting outputs. Spaced refusals score zero under the gold rule. Neither rule is human refusal accuracy. Train-only RAG excludes held-out source groups and target answers; low overlap is sparse-source transfer, not a test of ordinary answer-present RAG quality. LoRA training used 48 examples, 12 optimizer steps and 270,336 trainable parameters; no GPU comparison was executed.

figures.title: Prompt-similarity support and standardized lexical contrast
figures.caption: 127 question-neighbor pairs: 70 within and 57 across quarantine groups. Only the .40–<.70 bins have both strata, retaining 93 pairs (36 within, 57 cross);34 higher-similarity within-group pairs are excluded. Standardized means apply identical pooled-bin weights .5806/.2796/.1398 to the separate group means. The remaining .2972 versus .0442 contrast is descriptive; quarantine construction, within-bin topic/length differences and pair dependence prevent a causal reuse or answer-agreement interpretation. Grey bins have no cross-stratum support; missing means are null, not zero.
